newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian firms' div payment signals optimism-Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Indian firms' div payment signals optimism-Morgan.

text.p: Higher dividends announced by many Indian firms point to their optimism for the current year and beyond, U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said in an India strategy report on Wednesday.
"About one-fourth of Indian companies have declared higher dividends despite lower earnings in 1996/97 (April-March)," the report said.
"We also believe the announcement of bonus issues by companies with lower or flat earnings is a signal of better times ahead."
Morgan Stanley said a fourth of the companies that reported lower earnings declared increased dividends.
"A further 41 percent of the companies with lower earnings announced that they were maintaining their dividends at previous levels," the report said.
Higher dividends could also be in anticipation of shareholder demands as dividends are now tax-free for investors.
"Also, promoters might want to augment their personal cash flows through higher dividends," it said.
"With most companies having declared their FY1997 results, it is fairly clear that profitability has been affected by the deceleration in industrial growth," it said.
